title: Knowledge check: Setting Up the Development Environment

questions.prompt: In Setting Up the Development Environment, which statement best describes Installing a supported Node.js version?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Separate current Express 5 behavior from legacy Express 4 behavior. Confirm version-specific syntax against the migration guide and use regression tests instead of assuming compatibility.
Make the runtime version, module system, package scripts and lockfile explicit. A fresh installation should reproduce the same dependency graph and documented startup behavior.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
questions.answer_key: Separate current Express 5 behavior from legacy Express 4 behavior. Confirm version-specific syntax against the migration guide and use regression tests instead of assuming compatibility.
questions.explanation: Separate current Express 5 behavior from legacy Express 4 behavior. Confirm version-specific syntax against the migration guide and use regression tests instead of assuming compatibility.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Setting Up the Development Environment?
options: A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.

questions.prompt: A change related to Setting Up the Development Environment appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
